what_it_does: Pirate is a system for streaming high-quality VR video to mobile edge devices (phones, tablets) over extremely limited networks. The challenge: VR needs both eyes rendered (left and right views), which doubles the data, but networks at the edge are too slow. Pirate solves this by sending only one eye's view at a time, then using pre-computed depth maps (information about how far away objects are) and optical flow (how pixels move between frames) to synthesize the other eye on the device itself—using simple math, not heavy machine learning. By alternating which eye gets sent and reusing synthesized frames, the system achieves real-time 90-frames-per-second VR at bitrates as low as 0.1 bits per pixel (extremely compressed).
